title: A Pizza Crust Helped Crack the Gilgo Beach Killings

narration: A pizza crust thrown in a Manhattan trash can helped crack the Gilgo Beach killings.
shots.visual_description: gb7 midtown (night grade); gb7_suit (silhouette): stand -> present -> stand; gb7_suit (silhouette): stand (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'MANHATTAN · JANUARY 2023', callout 'THE PIZZA BOX'.

sources.claim_text: According to prosecutors' July 2023 bail application, on or about 26 January 2023 a surveillance team recovered a pizza box Heuermann threw into a garbage can on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan; the leftover crust was swabbed for DNA. This is a court-filing allegation, never tested at trial (he later pleaded guilty).

On 8 April 2026, before any trial, Heuermann pleaded guilty to seven murders (three counts of first-degree and four of second-degree murder) and admitted killing an eighth woman, Karen Vergata, with whose death he was never charged.

narration: For more than a decade, the case went cold.
shots.visual_description: gb7 dune road (dawn grade); detective (silhouette): stand -> arms_crossed -> bowed -> stand (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'LONG ISLAND · 2010-2022'.
shots.reconstruction_tag: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC ROAD, NOT A CRIME SCENE

sources.claim_text: The first remains in the case were found in December 2010; no one was charged until July 2023, more than a decade later.

narration: Then, in 2022, a new task force reopened the files.
Within weeks, it had a suspect.

overlays.text: The new task force flagged him / within about six weeks / of forming.

sources.claim_text: A multi-agency Gilgo Beach task force (Suffolk County Police, Sheriff, New York State Police, FBI) was formed in early 2022.
FUN FACT: within about six weeks of the task force forming (March 2022), a state investigator identified Heuermann as a possible suspect.

narration: Prosecutors said it began with a truck a witness saw in 2010.
It led the task force to a Manhattan architect: Rex Heuermann.
shots.visual_description: office day (cold grade); analyst: sit_type -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_read -> sit; camera push/pull; overlays: card 'PROSECUTORS' 2023 FILING: / A FIRST-GENERATION / CHEVROLET AVALANCHE / SEEN BY A WITNESS IN 2010', card 'LINKED BY THE TASK FORCE · 2022 / A MANHATTAN ARCHITECT / REX HEUERMANN'.

LINKED BY THE TASK FORCE · 2022 / A MANHATTAN ARCHITECT / REX HEUERMANN

sources.claim_text: According to the 2023 filing, a witness saw a first-generation Chevrolet Avalanche when one of the women (Amber Costello) disappeared in 2010; in March 2022 investigators linked Heuermann to that kind of truck, which he had owned. Allegation, attributed.
Rex Heuermann was a Manhattan architect with an office on Fifth Avenue in Midtown.

narration: Next, burner phones. Prosecutors said they reached victims and pinged near his office.
shots.visual_description: gb7 midtown (night grade); agent_b (silhouette): read -> stand -> point_up; agent_a (silhouette): stand -> read -> stand_tense (walks); keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: svg, label 'PHONE RECORDS'.

sources.claim_text: Prosecutors alleged that burner phones were used to contact the victims and that phone records placed them near his Midtown Manhattan office. Allegation from the 2023 filing.

narration: In January 2023, he tossed a pizza box into a Fifth Avenue trash can.
shots.visual_description: gb7 surveillance (night grade); gb7_suit (silhouette): stand -> present -> stand (walks); agent_a (silhouette): stand -> hand_to_face; detective (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense -> point -> stand_tense; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'FIFTH AVENUE · JAN 2023'.

sources.claim_text: Investigators kept Heuermann under surveillance for more than a year before the arrest.

According to prosecutors' July 2023 bail application, on or about 26 January 2023 a surveillance team recovered a pizza box Heuermann threw into a garbage can on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan; the leftover crust was swabbed for DNA. This is a court-filing allegation, never tested at trial (he later pleaded guilty).

narration: Prosecutors said the crust's DNA linked him to a hair found with a victim.
shots.visual_description: lab (cold grade); scientist: examine -> hands_together -> read; camera push/pull; overlays: label 'THE CRUST · SWABBED FOR DNA', card 'PROSECUTORS' 2023 FILING / MITOCHONDRIAL DNA LINK / HE 'CANNOT BE EXCLUDED' / NOT A NUCLEAR, UNIQUE MATCH'.

overlays.text: PROSECUTORS' 2023 FILING / MITOCHONDRIAL DNA LINK / HE 'CANNOT BE EXCLUDED' / NOT A NUCLEAR, UNIQUE MATCH

sources.claim_text: According to prosecutors' July 2023 bail application, on or about 26 January 2023 a surveillance team recovered a pizza box Heuermann threw into a garbage can on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan; the leftover crust was swabbed for DNA. This is a court-filing allegation, never tested at trial (he later pleaded guilty).

Prosecutors' 2023 filing said a lab compared mitochondrial DNA from the crust with a male hair recovered with victim Megan Waterman, and that Heuermann 'cannot be excluded'. This was a MITOCHONDRIAL DNA link, not a nuclear (unique) match; the defence said mitochondrial DNA is less precise.

narration: In July 2023, officers arrested him near his Manhattan office.
shots.visual_description: gb7 midtown (night grade); gb7_suit (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense -> hands_behind (walks); agent_b (silhouette): stand -> present (walks); agent_a (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'MIDTOWN · 13 JULY 2023', label 'PLEA IN 2023: NOT GUILTY'.

sources.claim_text: Heuermann was arrested on 13 July 2023 in Midtown Manhattan, near his office.
In July 2023 he pleaded not guilty (through his lawyer).

narration: In 2025, a judge allowed whole-genome DNA from hairs: reportedly a New York first.
shots.visual_description: lab (cold grade); examiner: examine -> stand -> arms_crossed; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'SEPTEMBER 2025 · DNA RULING', funfact 'It was reportedly the first time / a New York court allowed / whole-genome DNA from hair.'.

overlays.text: It was reportedly the first time / a New York court allowed / whole-genome DNA from hair.

sources.claim_text: FUN FACT: on 3 September 2025 Judge Timothy Mazzei ruled, after a Frye hearing, that whole-genome-sequencing (nuclear) DNA results from rootless hairs were admissible; reports described it as the first time such evidence was allowed in a New York court. It was a ruling on admissibility, not a finding of guilt.

sources.claim_text: On 8 April 2026, before any trial, Heuermann pleaded guilty to seven murders (three counts of first-degree and four of second-degree murder) and admitted killing an eighth woman, Karen Vergata, with whose death he was never charged.

narration: In June, he got three consecutive life sentences without parole.
shots.visual_description: courtroom (cold grade); official (silhouette): sit -> gavel -> sit -> sit_read; camera push/pull; overlays: card 'SENTENCED · 17 JUNE 2026 / 3 x LIFE WITHOUT PAROLE / + 4 x 25 YEARS TO LIFE / ALL CONSECUTIVE', stamp 'APPEAL WAIVED'.

overlays.text: SENTENCED · 17 JUNE 2026 / 3 x LIFE WITHOUT PAROLE / + 4 x 25 YEARS TO LIFE / ALL CONSECUTIVE

sources.claim_text: On 17 June 2026 he was sentenced to three consecutive terms of life without parole plus four consecutive terms of 25 years to life.
As part of the plea he waived his right to appeal.

narration: Eight women. Their families waited years for that day.
shots.visual_description: gb7 dune road (dawn grade); camera push/pull; overlays: svg.
shots.reconstruction_tag: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC ROAD, NOT A CRIME SCENE

sources.claim_text: The eight women: Maureen Brainard-Barnes, Melissa Barthelemy, Megan Waterman, Amber Costello, Jessica Taylor, Sandra Costilla, Valerie Mack and Karen Vergata.
Victims' relatives spoke at the June 2026 sentencing, years (in some cases decades) after the women disappeared.
